criteria.description: Terminology: five accurate definitions/analogies worth 2 each (1 meaning, 1 analogy with mapping).

In practice.py use sqlite3 to create a products table with id primary key, name, price and stock. Insert Pen 200/4, Book 500/8 and Bag 4000/0 using parameters. Mark: implementation/artefact meets stated requirements (6); demonstrated stated cases with actual output (3); explanation of the result (1).

Select name and stock ordered by id. Save the SQL and returned rows; do not use SELECT * for this exercise. Mark: implementation/artefact meets stated requirements (6); demonstrated stated cases with actual output (3); explanation of the result (1).

Select stock <=4 ordered by stock then id. Expect Bag then Pen. Repeat for threshold 0 using a bound parameter. Mark: implementation/artefact meets stated requirements (6); demonstrated stated cases with actual output (3); explanation of the result (1).

Change Pen stock to 7 with WHERE id=1. Show before/after rows and verify Book remains 8. Explain the effect of omitting WHERE. Mark: implementation/artefact meets stated requirements (6); demonstrated stated cases with actual output (3); explanation of the result (1).

Delete only the zero-stock Bag by ID. Show remaining row count 2. Work only on your disposable practice database. Mark: implementation/artefact meets stated requirements (6); demonstrated stated cases with actual output (3); explanation of the result (1).

Use SUM(price * stock) after the update/delete. Expect 5400. Define and demonstrate a zero result for an empty table using COALESCE. Mark: implementation/artefact meets stated requirements (6); demonstrated stated cases with actual output (3); explanation of the result (1).

Commit to inventory.sqlite3, close and reopen it, then show rows remain. Insert a name containing an apostrophe using parameters and demonstrate it reads back unchanged. Mark: implementation/artefact meets stated requirements (6); demonstrated stated cases with actual output (3); explanation of the result (1).
Independent verification: new normal case (3), boundary/failure case (3), reproducible commands and observed outputs (2), limitation and repair plan (2).
